pysnap.ssh package¶

ssh access to guests that have no console on COM1.

PySnap runs the system OpenSSH client (ssh) with its own key pair and its own known_hosts files, so the user’s keys and ~/.ssh/known_hosts are never read or changed.

Submodules¶

pysnap.ssh.client module¶

Run the system ssh client against a forwarded guest port.

Every call uses the PySnap key, the known_hosts file of the VM with StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new (the first key is trusted, a changed key is refused) and no user configuration (-F with the null device), so the behaviour does not depend on ~/.ssh. Non-interactive calls run in batch mode: they never ask for a password.

pysnap.ssh.client.install_script(public_key, *, with_root)[source]¶

Return the guest shell script that adds the PySnap key.

The key is appended to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys unless it is there already. With with_root, a user other than root then runs the same for root through su; the guest asks for the root password, and an empty or wrong one only skips root.

Parameters:

  • public_key (str) – Public key line.

  • with_root (bool) – Also install the key for root.

Returns:

Script for sh -c.

Return type:

str

pysnap.ssh.client.install_key_interactively(target, store)[source]¶

Log in with a password in the current terminal and add the key.

ssh asks for the password of target.user; the guest may ask for the root password. Nothing is captured, the user sees the whole dialogue.

Parameters:

pysnap.ssh.keys module¶

The PySnap ssh key pair and per-VM known_hosts files.

Everything lives in ~/.pysnap/ssh (mode 0700): the key pair pysnap_vm_access_ed25519 with its .pub file, created once by ssh-keygen without a passphrase, and known_hosts.d/<VM UUID>, one known_hosts file per VM. Both the directory and the file names are unique to PySnap, and existing files are never overwritten.
